critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict: The match is done properly. In handbags the three bags sit in the same order as in purses and on the same marks, and all three read whole and closed. The frame is still not pro level. The other five frames have not been re-rendered. Wide, overhead, tag, two_shot and empty are still the round-5 renders (commit 1e693ae), only regraded since under grade A fixed, so every round-5 fault still shows in them. Commit e13e009 has since changed the code behind several of those faults: the cap bands, the duffel lining, the officers' hand value, the tag card and the scanner's exit light. None of that is in the frames yet. The handbags frame has five problems of its own. (1) The figure behind the shoulder bag is Dawn. The top edge of the frame cuts her at the neck, just under the jaw, leaving a headless stone torso. Her pale lapels (about 85-92 graded) and pale blouse V (about 95-100) against a jacket of about 40 make it read as a man's dinner jacket. (2) Officer A's arm comes in from the top right and ends in a pale, palm-down claw about 12-16 px above the tote's handles. It grips nothing. The hand sits around 120 graded with peaks near 150, far brighter than the tote's body (77). (3) The light is even product light, not a lit island. The near bench top is the brightest large area in the frame: a flat grey slab over the lower third, graded median 125 (raw 165). At this grazing angle its brushing can read as wood grain. The frame mean is 61, against 26 for purses. (4) The tote's maker's plate is back. It is a pale debossed stamp just under the rim, about 14x7 px at x 985-999, y 269-276, and stands +19 graded above a 5 px blur. In purses the same spot is +4. (5) The colours have drifted from purses. The shoulder bag reads as lilac-grey nylon, not burgundy. The tote is a dusty pink-brown, not cognac. The black satchel's flap reads slate: about 100-112, against a body of 49. The scores are unchanged.
answers:
Q1. Are the bags in the same order, and in matching positions, as in purses? Yes. The shoulder bag is on the left, the satchel in the centre and the tote on the right. A 50/50 blend of the two graded frames shows no doubling. The satchel's and the tote's edges, the clasp and the handle tabs land on the same columns in both frames (for example the tote's left edge at 806-825 and the clasp at 625-657). The shoulder bag matches within about 5 px. The tote's handle apex sits at about y 130-135 in both. Turning the LAYOUT["three bags"] marks and the camera together 180 degrees about the bench centre worked.

Q2. Do all three read as intact? Yes, as objects. The shoulder bag is zipped, its pull hangs at the left and its strap is whole. The satchel's flap is closed and its clasp shut, and its crossbody strap loops down to the bench on the left. The tote is whole, with both handles and their tabs. All three sit down on the bench with contact shadows. Three things in this frame do not match purses or the film's rules.
(a) The tote shows a stamp: a pale debossed maker's plate at x 985-999, y 269-276, about 14x7 px. It stands +19 graded (+26 raw) above a 5 px blur. In purses the same spot is +4, which is noise. props.remove_tote_plate() runs in load_props(), but it does not remove what this camera sees. The kit's rule is no badges or brands in the film (props.py), so it has to go.
(b) The shoulder bag grades to about (68-74, 66-73, 74-81), a cool lilac-grey, and its crinkled surface reads as nylon. In purses it is about (61-67, 53-58, 55-59), a burgundy leather. There are two causes. PROPS here grades it at sat 0.55, val 0.5, where evidence_table's BAG_GRADE uses sat 0.8, val 0.55. And the troffer is cool, where the purses lamp is warm (WARM = (1.0, 0.85, 0.68)). Cut between the two frames and it looks like a different bag.
(c) The tote grades to about (90-93, 68-71, 65-67), with blue close to green: a dusty salmon-pink. In purses it is about (64-67, 46-48, 30-31), cognac. PROPS here uses sat 1.02, val 0.67, hue 0.49, against BAG_GRADE's 1.0, 0.84, 0.50, and the light is cooler; the raw tote is (144, 82, 60). Under the troffer's sheen the black satchel's flap grades to about 100-112 against a body of 49, so it reads slate.

Q3. Do the figures behind leave the bags clear? Nothing crosses a bag, so strictly yes. Four things still crowd them.
(a) The frame cuts Dawn at the neck, just under the jaw: the pale strip at rows 0-5, x 364-412. The frame's top edge points out almost level (about +0.6 degrees), so at her distance it passes about 1.36 m up. Moving her back raises the cut by only about 1 cm per metre, so she stays headless at any distance.
(b) The shoulder bag's strap overlaps her. Its apex and right leg lie over her arm and jacket; the right leg separates only by a lit edge of about 60-90 against a jacket of 30-45. Its left leg runs parallel to the edge of her upper arm from y 100 to 250, about 25-45 px outside it, over the dark wall. It is a busy tangle.
(c) The satchel's left side and its strap hardware sit on Dawn's hip and skirt at nearly the same value. At x 500-555, y 360-400 the bag is at 49-59 and the skirt at 55-58, so the satchel's left contour dissolves there.
(d) Officer A's hand hangs 12-16 px above the tote's handle apex (its underside at about y 118, the handles from y 131). The near-tangent draws the eye, and the hand is the brightest thing above the bags. The cause is in _reach_point("tote_handle"): it puts the palm at hi.z + 0.052, so the hand hovers by design.
Two pale bits of set dressing also peek out round the tote. The edge of the bench glove box shows at x 1164-1172, y 270-330, at 37-60 against 10-26. A nearly white corner of the clipboard sheet, up to about 205 graded, shows between the satchel and the tote at x 789-818, y 341-358.

Stage: the other five frames are still the round-5 renders, and these faults still show in them. The caps are seated at the front only, with pale skull showing under the back of the band in two_shot. Officer A's hand in the overhead is white and splayed (about 165-195 graded). The open duffel's interior is lighter than its outside (55 against 38). The overhead's tote reads mustard. The scanner is a grey box whose right side sits at 4-7 graded (0-3 raw). Its monitor reads as a pale card (about 96 graded in the wide). The tag is a neutral near-white card (graded 182, 184, 180) on thin, wire-like twine.
The code has moved since then. e13e009 fits a cap band to each head, darkens the duffel lining to about 0.012 with zip lips and tape, drops the officers' hand value to 0.14, and adds the scanner's exit bounce light, service door and pilot lamp. It also sets the tag card to (0.50, 0.40, 0.26) and thickens the twine to 0.45 mm.

Continuity: the coverage plan cuts the overhead ("The discovery, from above") straight to handbags ("The handbags under the cold light"). Along the bench the bags keep the same order: tote toward -X, shoulder bag toward the scanner. Their places and turns differ, though. In handbags the trio sits about 0.32 m further toward -X, so the tote stands where the open duffel's end lies in the overhead. Each bag is turned about 110-130 degrees differently. The duffel is gone. As things stand, the two do not cut together.

fixes.problem: The top edge of the frame cuts Dawn at the neck, just under the jaw: a headless torso in the top-left third. Her pale lapels (about 85-92 graded) and blouse V (about 95-100) against a jacket of about 40 make it read as a man's dinner jacket. The frame's top edge points out almost level (about +0.6 degrees), so moving her back raises the cut by only about 1 cm per metre. She has to leave the frame.
fixes.fix: Take her out of this camera. In CAMERAS["handbags"]["cheat"], add "Dawn": (1.75, -1.10). That is beyond the bench's +X end, and her nearest edge then projects about 660 px past the frame's left edge. Confirm in the render that no shadow of hers lands on the bench. Alternatively hide her: in apply_camera(), after the loop that resets the cast's hide_render, set hide_render=True on Dawn's holder and all its children_recursive when name == "handbags". The next call's loop restores her for the other cameras. Behind the shoulder bag the background is then the block wall, which grades about 15-28 now on the left. Do not keep her by raising the camera to crop at the chest. That needs a camera about 0.25 m higher, looking about 26 degrees down, and it breaks the purses match. If she must stay for another reason, darken her lapels and blouse. The lapel facing is written at (0.067, 0.052, 0.041), about 2.2x the jacket's 0.030 umber; take it to about 1.15x. Take the blouse from 0.098 to about 0.06. The torso then stops reading as a tuxedo.

fixes.camera: handbags (and overhead, which uses the same reach)
fixes.problem: Officer A's arm comes in from the top right and ends in a pale, palm-down claw about 12-16 px above the tote's handle apex. It grips nothing and sits near-tangent to the handles. The hand grades around 120 with peaks near 150 (raw median about 185), well above the tote's body (77). The cause is in _reach_point("tote_handle"): it puts the palm at hi.z + 0.052, so with the cheat to (-0.52, 0.55) the hand hovers by design.
fixes.fix: Make it a real grip or take it out. To grip: add a reach kind "tote_grip" to _reach_point(). Take the tote's mesh vertices in world space with z > hi.z - 0.012, use their mean XY as the handle apex, and aim the palm at (apex.x, apex.y, hi.z + 0.016). Give OfficerA "reach_r": "tote_grip", "fingers": 72, "close_thumb": True, so the fingers pass under and round both handles. Put this in POSES["ch05"] itself, because the overhead uses the same reach, or else in a camera-only pose (CAMERAS["handbags"]["pose"] = "ch05 grip", POSES["ch05 grip"] = dict(POSES["ch05"], OfficerA={...})). Accept the solve only if the report prints a palm error under 10 mm. Then confirm in the render that the fingertips hide behind the far handle and the knuckles sit on top. The hand's value: it renders at raw 120-210 despite hands_stone(value=0.14). Print the resolved colour of the 'stone at hands' mix for OfficerA's body material, check that its output is linked to Base Color and that the handmask covers the hand, and fix the link if it does not land. Aim for 60-80 graded. To take it out instead (the fallback, and the cleaner match to purses, which has no hands): give this camera a pose where OfficerA has {"behind": True, "look": "handbag-tote"} and no reach_r. His body already projects off the right edge, so no arm then enters the frame.

fixes.problem: This is product light, not a lit island. The near bench top is the brightest large area in the frame: a flat grey slab over the lower third, graded median 125 (about 80-150) at (100-700, 560-700), raw median 165. It is brighter than every bag. At this grazing angle its brushing can read as wood grain. The frame mean is 61, against 26 for purses, so the plate has none of the noir falloff.
fixes.fix: Shade the near bench for this camera only. Option A: a shadow-only flag, a plane 'handbags_flag' of about 1.4 x 0.4 m at z = TOP + 1.05, long side along X, centred near x 0.45. It must not be seen by the camera or in reflections, so set visible_camera, visible_glossy and visible_transmission to False. Show it only when name == 'handbags', toggled in apply_camera() the way tag_rake and floor_return are. The tote's front reaches about y 0.26 and the bags' fronts take their light from the troffer's +Y half. So start the flag's inner edge at about y 0.30, over the strip between the bench's back edge (y 0.40) and the bags, and bring it in only as far as the bags' values allow. Option B: light-link the bench top out of troffer_bench_light for this camera, and give it a weaker linked copy, as floor_return does for the floor. Either way, the target is the near bench at 45-65 graded at (100-700, 560-700), the bags' fronts at their current values, and the tote as the strongest mass in the frame. For this camera, also set 'bench top steel' Anisotropic from 0.34 to about 0.15 and narrow its roughness range from (0.38, 0.46) to about (0.40, 0.44). Set the node inputs in apply_camera() and restore them for the other cameras, so the top reads as brushed steel, not wood.

fixes.problem: The tote's maker's plate shows: a pale debossed stamp at x 985-999, y 269-276, +19 graded (+26 raw) over a 5 px blur. In purses the same spot is +4. props.remove_tote_plate() runs in load_props() but misses what this camera sees. The kit's rule is no badges or brands in the film (props.py).
fixes.fix: Find the stamp on the model. Build a BVHTree from the tote mesh in world space. Cast rays from the handbags camera through pixels (985-999, 269-276), using camera.data.view_frame and the render resolution. Print the hits in the first mesh child's local space, and the UVs at the hits (face loops plus barycentric weights). Then, inside this stage's own module (props.py is shared), call props._retouch_tote_textures(h, box, dx) with a texel box of about 100x90 round that UV, and props._smooth_tote_plate(h, local_hit, 0.02). If this is a different oval from the one already removed, run both. Check: the high-pass peak in that box (luminance minus a 5 px Gaussian blur) is at or below 6 graded.

fixes.problem: The bag colours have drifted from purses. The shoulder bag grades to about (68-74, 66-73, 74-81), a lilac-grey nylon, against burgundy (61-67, 53-58, 55-59). The tote grades to about (90-93, 68-71, 65-67), a dusty salmon-pink, against cognac (64-67, 46-48, 30-31). The satchel's flap grades to about 100-112 against a body of 49, so the black bag reads slate. Part of the cause is the stage's own prop grade, and part is the cool troffer against the purses' warm lamp.
fixes.fix: Use evidence_table's BAG_GRADE for the bags: shoulder sat 0.8, val 0.55; tote sat 1.0, val 0.84, hue 0.50. Both modules then share one prop grade. For this light only, cut the sheen. The tote's raw blue of about 60 is cool troffer sheen, so take FINISH['handbag-tote'] spec from 0.4 to about 0.22 and raise its rough_add from 0.2 to about 0.32. Raise the satchel's rough_add from 0.12 to about 0.28. Targets in the graded handbags frame: the tote's body about (100-115, 72-80, 45-55); the shoulder bag with R at least G+8 and R at least B+6; the satchel's flap at or below 75. If the cool troffer still keeps the bags off target, push this stage's tote and shoulder grade further toward warm rather than changing the film grade. Re-check the overhead's tote afterwards, which currently reads mustard.

fixes.problem: There are edge merges and slivers round the bags. The satchel's left side and its strap hardware sit on Dawn's skirt at the same value (bag 49-59, skirt 55-58 at x 500-555, y 360-400). The edge of the glove box shows to the right of the tote (x 1164-1172, y 270-330). A nearly white corner of the clipboard sheet, up to about 205 graded, shows between the satchel and the tote (x 789-818, y 341-358).
fixes.fix: The satchel merge goes once Dawn is out (fix 1). In apply_camera(), after set_beat() (which resets the dressing), when cfg.get('layout') == 'three bags', hide the objects in _STATE['dressing'] whose names start with 'bench_gloves' or 'bench_clipboard'. Do not slide them instead. The clipboard at (-0.80, -0.30) would overlap the glove box, and the glove box at x -0.95 would overhang the bench's end at -1.0. Then check that no pale shape touches a bag's silhouette.

fixes.problem: These frames have not been re-rendered since round 5. Officer A's white, splayed hand is the brightest thing on the tote (about 165-195 graded). The duffel's interior is lighter than its outside (55 against 38). The tote reads mustard. The caps are seated at the front only, with pale skull showing under the back of the band in profile. The code for the caps, the lining and the hand value changed after these renders (e13e009), so the frames do not show it. The overhead and handbags are cut back to back in the coverage plan, and the bags are not in the same places between them.
fixes.fix: Re-render overhead, wide and two_shot with the current code first. That brings in fit_cap_band(), the open_zip() lining at about 0.012 with its zip lips and tape, the hand value of 0.14 and the current tote grade. Then check that the cap bands sit on the head all round, that the duffel's opening reads darker than its outside, and that the hand sits at 60-80 graded. The handbags render, made with this code, still shows the hand at raw 120-210, so do fix 2's hand-value check and grip in POSES["ch05"]. For the continuity cut, the order along the bench already matches, but the places and turns do not. Option A: move the 'three bags' marks and the handbags camera together by about +0.32 m in X. This is a rigid move, so the purses match holds. Copy the shifted marks and their turns (342, 333, 325) into LAYOUT['ch05'] for the three handbags. Check in the overhead that the tote clears the duffel (about 8 cm). Check in handbags whether the open duffel at (-0.53, 0.02) shows behind the tote; if it does, it belongs there. Option B: put a shot that does not show the bench between the two beats in the coverage plan.

fixes.problem: These frames have not been re-rendered since round 5. The scanner is a grey box whose right side sits at 4-7 graded (0-3 raw). Its nine curtain strips read as one flat, evenly ruled panel. Its monitor reads as a pale card (about 96 graded in the wide) with no visible spill, although the bezel and a 9 W 'mon_spill' are already in these renders. The tag is a neutral near-white card (graded 182, 184, 180) on a thin twine that reads as wire, although the lark's-head two-ply jute is already in the code. Since these renders, e13e009 has added a 12 W 'scanner exit bounce', a service door, a kick plate and a pilot lamp, the (0.50, 0.40, 0.26) manila card and a 0.45 mm twine.
fixes.fix: Re-render wide, empty and tag with the current code before changing anything else. Then check four things. Does the scanner's right side lift above about 10 graded? Does the tag card grade buff, with R clearly above B? Does the twine read as fibre rather than wire? Does the screen read as a dark bezel round a dimmer blank screen, with a pool of spill on the housing's flank? For whatever still fails: add a Bevel modifier of about 1.5-2 cm, limited by angle, to the generated scanner housing in inspection_room_xray.py. Give the curtain strips a few more degrees of swing and stagger their lengths, so their edges catch the light. Lower the screen's glow from 1.1 and raise mon_spill until the spill shows, keeping the screen blank. Thicken the twine's plies, or add a fibre bump, until it no longer reads as wire.
